subject: QBR prep: prioritization matrix, customer heatmap & exec attention items
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR prep: prioritization matrix, customer heatmap & exec attention items

Team —

Attached is the first-pass customer heatmap for Acme (pdf) and a prioritization matrix (xlsx) I pulled together for the QBR next Wed. High-level observations: 

- Health signal: Usage stable, but 2-week drop in inference throughput for their analytics pipelines (see row 3 of heatmap).
- Support churn risk: Elevated error-rate spikes correlated with a model roll last month; CSM notes rising ticket volume.
- Contract: Renewal Q3; procurement has open questions about data retention and SLA credits (we got the redline in March).

Asks: 
1) Can Sales confirm procurement timeline and whether we have the latest SOW/Redlines? (Aditya)
2) Engineering: quick read on the throughput regression root cause and whether there's a temporary mitigation we can present. (Lauren + Eng)
3) Exec attention: We should flag two items for the QBR slide deck — potential SLA credit ask, and a proposed canary rollback to prior model variant.

I've annotated the matrix with a preliminary R/A/G and impact estimate. I propose we prioritize items that materially affect latency and data retention compliance. I'll own the slide for "Exec Attention" but need short bullets from each owner by EOD so we can finalize the deck.

Attachments: customer-heatmap-20270425.pdf, qbr-prioritization-matrix.xlsx

— Mina
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: prioritization matrix, customer heatmap & exec attention items

Thanks Mina — good work. A few quick notes: 

- I agree with flagging SLA credit and canary rollback. Add a short "business impact" line for each (revenue exposed, customer sentiment).
- Exec attendees: recommend including VP Sales (Aditya), Head of Product (Marissa), and CTO (I'll request but confirm).
- For the slide deck, I can provide the customer-facing summary and one-line mitigation options.

Quick asks for owners by EOD: 
- Aditya: procurement timing and whether Acme expects a formal PO/POC by mid-May.
- Eng (cc'd via separate thread if needed): confirmation on rollback feasibility and expected recovery time.

On the heatmap: can someone double-check the annotations in row 3 — I think the throughput dip aligns with the 2027-03-18 model push. If true, that strengthens the rollback case.

— Lauren
VP, Customer Success (acting)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: keith.alvarez@acme.com
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 12:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: prioritization matrix, customer heatmap & exec attention items

Looping in procurement context and timeline. 

- Acme procurement has indicated they want final T&Cs and an updated exhibit on data retention before the renewal conversation. They asked for our response to the redline by May 10.
- I've confirmed with account exec that finance expects legal to sign off on a one-year renewal; no expansion at present.
- Risk: if we can't close T&Cs before their internal budget cutoff (June 1), expansion and pricing leverage could be impacted.

Action items: 
1) Legal/Contracts: finalize response to redline by 2027-05-08 (I'll follow up offline).
2) Product & Eng: short note on rollback vs patch plan for the throughput regression (one paragraph).
3) Mina: I'll draft the procurement timeline slide and add the HubSpot deal link below.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345

— Aditya
Sr. Director, Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, keith.alvarez@acme.com
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: prioritization matrix, customer heatmap & exec attention items

Thanks all. Adding a brief product perspective and next steps for the QBR: 

- Root cause: preliminary triage shows a model variant combination that increased KV cache misses under Acme's long-sequence workload. We can mitigate by reverting the variant for their production pool while we backfill a quantized kernel that addresses the cache behavior. Estimated timeline: rollback = same-day during a maintenance window; kernel fix = 2-3 weeks.
- Customer comms: recommend we present a two-path plan in the QBR — (A) immediate rollback + monitoring, (B) risk-tolerant path with kernel backfill and performance validation.

I'll draft the one-paragraph mitigation and a short timing table for Mina's slides. 

Keith (cc): can you confirm whether Acme prefers a rollback during your maintenance window (Thu nights) or a mid-day slot? We want to minimize disruption.

— Marissa
Head of Product
Redwood Inference
